sentiment.rationale: The document reports that 2025 results matched prior guidance (organic revenue growth in line with long-term algorithm, comparable EPS of $3). Forward guidance for 2026 is for organic revenue growth of 4%-5% and comparable currency-neutral EPS growth of 5%-6%, which is in line with the long-term growth algorithm and not raised above prior expectations. Management expresses confidence but also flags specific headwinds (Mexico excise tax, divestiture impacts, weaker consumer demand in China/India). The overall forward signal is modestly positive but not a material raise, warranting a score near the lower end of the positive range.

summary.revenue: Organic revenue growth of 5% in Q4 2025 and 7% average annual organic revenue growth since 2017. Full-year 2025 organic revenue growth in line with long-term growth algorithm.
summary.eps: Comparable earnings per share reached $3 in 2025, growing 4% despite a 5-point currency headwind and a 2-point increase in the comparable effective tax rate.
summary.guidance: For 2026: organic revenue growth of 4%-5%; comparable currency-neutral earnings per share growth of 5%-6% (excluding M&A); comparable EPS growth of 7%-8% versus $3 in 2025. Currency tailwinds of 1 point to net revenues and 3 points to EPS. Divestiture headwinds of approximately 4 points to net revenues and 1 point to EPS.
summary.margin: Comparable gross margin and comparable operating margin both increased approximately 50 basis points in Q4 2025, driven by underlying expansion partially offset by currency headwinds. North America achieved 30% operating margin for the first time.
key_risks: New excise tax in Mexico implemented at the start of 2026, expected volume pressure despite mitigation plans.
Consumer demand in major markets like China and India did not recover to pre-pandemic levels.
Revenue and profit declined in Asia Pacific during Q4 due to softer consumer spending, weaker industry performance and cycling strong growth in the prior year.
Divestitures (sale of Coca-Cola Beverages Africa and CHI Nigeria) will be a back-half weighted headwind to net revenue and EPS in 2026.
Continued macroeconomic pressure on lower-income consumers in North America.
key_opportunities: Value share gains for the nineteenth consecutive quarter in 2025.
North America achieved 30% operating margin for the first time, with volume, revenue, and comparable operating income all increasing.
Innovation contributions (Sprite Chill, Coca-Cola Holiday Creamy Vanilla) and strong performance of brands like fairlife, BODYARMOR, Powerade.
Planned investments in innovation, digital engagement, and expanding billion-dollar brands.
World Cup in Mexico in 2026 as a marketing opportunity.
Currency tailwinds expected in 2026 (1 point to net revenues, 3 points to EPS).

management_tone.label: confident
management_tone.justification: Management expresses confidence in the outlook, with James Quincey stating 'we are well positioned, I think, to achieve our objectives both in 2026 and the long term' and Henrique Braun saying 'I'm confident we will deliver on our 2026 guidance and capture the vast opportunities available.'
